The learner asks specifically: Make sure one of the senses is this meaning: to move something towards you.

draft.shortGloss: to pull; to tug; to work (colloquial)
draft.emotion: assertive and direct, putting effort into a physical task
notes: In Mexico, 'jalar' is the standard verb for 'to pull'.
In many other parts of the Spanish-speaking world, you will hear 'tirar' instead.
Colloquially in Mexico, 'jalar' can also mean 'to work' (e.g., 'el coche ya jala' means 'the car works now').

senses.definition: To move something towards you by pulling.

examples.text: Tienes que jalar la puerta para abrirla.
examples.translation: You have to pull the door to open it.
examples.emotion: helpful and instructional, pointing out how something works

senses.definition: To function or work, often used for machines or electrical devices.

examples.text: Mi computadora vieja ya no jala bien.
examples.translation: My old computer doesn't work well anymore.
examples.emotion: frustrated and annoyed, lamenting a broken device
examples.note: Commonly used in Mexico to describe whether appliances or gadgets are operational.
